the border is preserved (visible aerated lung rim separates the opacity from the heart) or obscured (opacity merges with/blends into the heart contour).", "Apply the silhouette sign: A preserved border indicates the lesion is not in direct contact with the mediastinal pleura/pericardium (e.g., peripheral lung, posterior lower lobe), whereas an obscured border indicates direct anatomical contact (e.g., middle lobe, lingula, or anterior segment of the lower lobe)."]}, {"category": "localization", "trigger": "When evaluating the distribution of pulmonary opacities on a chest X-ray to zones (apical, mid, lower) and radial position (central/perihilar vs. peripheral/subpleural).", "Distinguish apical predominance (typically associated with sarcoidosis or tuberculosis) from lower-zone or peripheral predominance (often seen in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis or organizing pneumonia) by comparing opacity intensity across these specific regions."]}]

C) Tracheomegaly with multiple well-defined opacities in the right lower lobe and increased linear opacities in the left pulmonary base.
D) Tracheomegaly with multiple ill-defined opacities in the left upper lobe and increased linear opacities in the right pulmonary base.
